To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The puffing of Balbiani rings in Chironomus larvae is dependent on the protein synthesis.
(i) protein synthesis is required for the maintenance of a given Balbiani ring (BR) puffing state; and (ii) selective reactivation of collapsed BRs can be induced by protein synthesis inhibition.

“In the mid-IV instar larvae of Chironoms thummi, BR2 re-expansion induced by cycloleximide or anisomycin in galactose-untreated larvae and by cyclolexime or anisomycine alone in galactose-treated larvae suggests that the maintenance of the BR2 repressed state is dependent on the presence of newly synthesized proteins”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible involvement of newly synthesized proteins in puffing regulation.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the puffing of Balbiani rings.
the analysis of a possible dependence of puff expansion and repression on the synthesis of specific proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BR1 puffing state depends on the synthesis of a factor which is required for its maintenance, whereas BR2 puffing state is maintained by a repressor-like factor, the synthesis of which would be inhibited by the galactoses.
the puffing states are determined by the balance between activator and repressor activities.
puffing of the BRs is dependent on protein synthesis, but this dependence is not necessarily the same in all the cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BRs are not only sensitive to protein synthesis inhibition but they also show different sensitivities to this kind of treatment.

, in C. thummi, the puffing state of a given BR is determined by the balance of activities of two factors: a positive one, which is probably constitutive, and a negative one, which is induced by galactose treatment.

BR puffing is a dynamic process in which the puffing states of BR1 and BR 2 are maintained by the balance of two antagonistic factors, the repressor and the activator, the latter being dependent on the protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of the BRs, the puffing state can result from a balance between the activities of two different types of regulatory factors, one promoting the puffing and one suppressing it.
the protein synthesis inhibition can be exploited as a tool for the study of the puffing mechanisms.
the puffing states can be maintained in a stable way by the supply of new proteins.
